newsitem.title: MEXICO: Opposition ahead Mexico City governor race - survey.
newsitem.headline: Opposition ahead Mexico City governor race - survey.

text.p: Two Mexican opposition parties are ahead of the ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) in voter preferences for the governorship of Mexico City, a survey revealed Wednesday.

The pro-business National Action Party (PAN) and the leftist Democratic Revolution Party (PRD) both have more support than the PRI in a pre-election poll carried out by the respected Opinion Studies Centre of Guadalajara University.

Of 820 people of voting age polled February 1-2 in Mexico City, 42.9 percent said they would vote for the PAN, 23.5 percent for the PRD and 17.5 percent for the PRI. The margin of error was plus or minus 3.4 percent.

Mexico City residents will for the first time vote for a governor this July 6. Traditionally, the Mexican president has hand picked the head of the metropolis, which has in the past been the post of mayor.

Those polled said the main reason for the swing against the ruling party was for a change in power. The PRI has held the presidency, congressional majorities and most of the country's governorships for the past 66 years.
The Opinion Studies Centre said in a media conference that those voters polled who said they still preferred the PRI did so out of "tradition".
But on specific candidates, 36.7 percent of those who opted for the PAN said they preferred none of the pre-candidates put forward, the survey said.
Top candidate for the PAN with 34 percent was Diego Fernandez, the firebrand politician who was defeated by Ernesto Zedillo in the 1994 presidency race.

For the PRD, 39.7 percent of those opting for the left-wing party said they preferred none of the pre-candidates standing. Cuauhtemoc Cardenas, whose father is a past president, obtained 26.5 percent and former party leader Porfirio Munoz Ledo took 15.4 percent.
A majority 54.4 percent of those opting for the PRI said they preferred none of the candidates.
